transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… well, occupational health sent me over. They’re making a big thing about my weight, saying it’s dangerously low for the kind of work I do—running presses, fabrication, being on my feet all day.

I don’t know, I honestly thought I was just getting leaner. More disciplined, I guess. At the shop, people are always talking about stamina and keeping up with the younger guys, and the machines don’t exactly wait for you, you know? I’ve worked around metal and plastic long enough to know you can’t be sloppy. But they said I needed to be seen, so… here I am.
Have you been eating less than usual lately, or have you been intentionally trying to lose weight?

I mean… I guess I have been keeping it pretty light. Most days before the early shift I just have coffee, because if I eat first I feel sluggish, and then at lunch maybe half a protein bar if I remember.

After work I’ve been doing yoga, and then I’ll have, like, a small bowl of vegetables. It sounds bad when I say it out loud, but it feels manageable that way. If I eat more than that, the whole day starts to feel… I don’t know, out of control. Like everything gets messy, and I need things to stay tight.
Do you worry about gaining weight or feel like your body is larger than it actually is?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t like saying it like that, because it sounds kind of ridiculous, but if the scale goes up even a tiny bit I just—my chest gets tight and I start thinking I’m slipping.

Like, at work if a measurement is off by even a hair, you know something’s wrong with the setup, and I guess I treat my weight like that too. If it moves up, I panic that I’m going to lose all the control I worked for and end up heavy again. So… yes, I do worry about it.
Have you been doing anything else, like exercising a lot or making yourself sick, to keep your weight down?

I… I’m not totally sure what counts as “a lot,” I guess. I mean, I do yoga after work, but it’s also kind of the only time everything gets quiet, if that makes sense. The shop is loud all day—presses, forklifts beeping, everyone yelling over the machines—and then you get home and your body’s still sort of vibrating.

As for making myself sick… I don’t know. I don’t really want to get into something that maybe isn’t… I mean, I’m not sure what you’re asking exactly. I just try to keep things controlled. Like if I stick to a routine, I feel less panicky. But, um… yeah, mostly I just try to keep moving and not let things get sloppy.

No features of bulimia or other specified feeding or eating disorders were endorsed. The symptoms do not appear to be better explained by another mental disorder or medical condition.
